div.head: Leis Wl 5
div.ab: Cil ki aveir rescut, u chevals u bos u vaches u berbiz u pors, que est forfeng apelé en Engleis, cil kis claimed, durrad pur la rescussiun VIII den., ja tant n’i ait, mes qu’il i oust cent almaille, ne durrad que VIII den.;

Cil ki aveir escut, u chivalz u buefs u vaches u porcs u berbiz, que est forfeng en Engleis apeled, cil qil clamed, durrad al gr[efe?] s[ive?] al provost aveir pur l’escuss[iun] VIII den., ja tant n’i ait, meis qu’il out cent almaille, ne durrad que VIII den.;

De aueriis, que prepositus hundredi restare fecerit. Si prepositus hundredi equos aut boues aut oues aut porcos uel cuiuscumque generis aueria uagantia restare fecerit, is qui ueniens sua clamauerit dabit preposito

Cil ki aveir rescut, u chevals u bos u vaches u berbiz u pors, que est forfeng apelé en Engleis, cil kis claimed durrad pur la rescussiun VIII den., ja tant n'i ait, mes qu'il i oust cent almaille ne durrad que VIII den.;

5. Derjenige, der Vieh rettend festgenommen hat, entweder Pferde oder Ochsen oder Kühe oder Schafe oder Schweine — was auf Englisch Forfang heisst: wer sie [als Eigenthümer] beansprucht, soll für die rettende Festnahme ([dem Reeve oder? I] dem Vogt [der Hundertschaft L] IL) 8 Pfennig (an Vieh I) geben; es sei dabei noch so viel [an Vieh], wenn es selbst 100 [Stück] Rindvieh wäre, er braucht nur 8 Pfennig zu geben;

5. He who has seized cattle by rescue, either horses or oxen or cows or sheep or pigs — which in English is called forfang: whoever claims them [as owner] shall give for the rescuing seizure ([to the reeve or? I] to the bailiff [of the hundred L] IL) 8 pennies (in cattle I); however much [cattle] there be, even if it were 100 [head of] cattle, he need only give 8 pennies;

If anyone has taken livestock into his care, whether horses or oxen or cows or sheep or pigs—in English called "forfang"—the man who claims them shall pay 8 pence in return for the care taken of them; however many there are up to a hundred head of cattle, he shall not give more than 8 pence.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 256–257 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 496–497, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Seizure of lost cattle. In Forfang, above p. 388, as in Hk, no official is mentioned

Vgl. Gl Einfang 2. 6a. Über die Ausdrücke s. Ducange excutere, reexc.; Godefroy escoudre, escorre, resco(u)rre, rescousse, rescussiun. Das anlautende r lässt Bartsch zugunsten der Lesart I konsequent fort.—L versteht zu eng nur verirrtes Vieh.—Das Räubern Abgejagte stellen neben Fund auch andere Germanen; J. Hübner Fund im Germ. Recht 96

Cf. Gl Einfang 2. 6a. On the expressions see Ducange excutere, reexc.; Godefroy escoudre, escorre, resco(u)rre, rescousse, rescussiun. Bartsch consistently omits the initial r in favour of the reading of I.—L too narrowly understands only stray cattle.—Other Germanic peoples too place what has been recovered from robbers alongside things found; J. Hübner Fund im Germ. Recht 96

Ursprünglich gewann der Einfänger den Einfanglohn und behielt, wie der Finder das Fundstück, das Vieh, bis es der Eigentümer einfordert. Das Eintreten des Beamten (der in c. 6 fehlt) laut IL bedeutet spätere Entwicklung. Letzterer fungiert auch Hu 4. ECf 24. Maitland Coll. popers II 72 nimmt an, der Fund (s. d. Gl 2; Vogt 17a) sei dem Eigentümer von Amts wegen übergeben

Originally the captor earned the fee for seizure and, like the finder with the thing found, kept the cattle until the owner claimed them. The intervention of the official (who is absent in c. 6) according to IL indicates a later development. The latter also acts in Hu 4. ECf 24. Maitland Coll. popers II 72 assumes that the thing found (see that word in Gl 2; Vogt 17a) was handed over to the owner by the authorities
Richtig Littré Dict. s. v. aumailles; vgl. Wb: animal. Frühere trennten al maille, was man vergeblich zu deuten suchte.—Vgl. Gl Busse 7
Correctly Littré Dict. s. v. aumailles; cf. Wb: animal. Earlier scholars divided it as al maille, which they tried in vain to interpret.—Cf. Gl Busse 7
